title: Fire and forget
sub: Fire-and-forget, a missing await and async void
cards/0/body:
Calling an async method without await is called fire-and-forget. The compiler warns you (CS4014).

The danger: you won't know when it finished, and you won't see its error.
cards/1/explain: The saves were started but never awaited. Their errors will be lost.
cards/2/q: What ends up in the log?
cards/2/options/0: "saved", even though the saves are still running or have already failed
cards/2/options/2: The log entry appears after all the saves
cards/2/explain: Without await, the code doesn't wait for SaveAsync to finish.
cards/3/body: An exception from async void goes to the SynchronizationContext where the method started. If there's no context (console, pool), it's thrown on the thread pool, and the process crashes.
cards/4/q: A console app calls an async void method that throws after an await. What happens?
cards/4/options/0: The process crashes with an unhandled exception
cards/4/options/2: A try around the call catches it
cards/4/explain: The call already returned, and the try around it finished long ago. Nobody is there to catch the exception.
cards/5/title: If you really must fire and forget
cards/5/body: Wrap the task so its error is sure to reach the log. On a server, use a BackgroundService or a queue for background work.
cards/6/q: What's wrong with fire-and-forget? Select all that apply.
cards/6/options/0: You can't tell when the task finished
cards/6/options/2: The task can outlive the object or request that started it
cards/6/explain: Speed is the same; it's all about control.
cards/7/pairs/1/1: Can't be awaited; an exception crashes the process
